# SASE

> Documentation pages, organized by the site's top-level sections.

## Home

- [Structured Agentic Software Engineering](https://sase.sh/) — Run, review, and land work from parallel coding agents in one terminal workspace.

## Get started

- [Make and review a change](https://sase.sh/start/first-change/) — Ask an agent for one small edit in SASE's demo workspace and inspect the resulting diff.
- [Run your first agent](https://sase.sh/start/first-run/) — Launch a read-only request in SASE's demo workspace and inspect the result.
- [Get started](https://sase.sh/start/) — Set up SASE, run an agent in its demo workspace, and review your first change.
- [Install and set up SASE](https://sase.sh/start/install/) — Install SASE, confirm the command works, and check that an agent provider is ready.

## Guides

- [Add an existing repository](https://sase.sh/guides/add-existing-repository/) — Register a repository you already have as a SASE project and initialize it.
- [Choose providers and models](https://sase.sh/guides/choose-providers-models/) — Install a provider CLI, check authentication, and pick the model agents use.
- [Configure the essentials](https://sase.sh/guides/configure-essentials/) — Set the handful of configuration values most setups change, and find the rest.
- [Diagnose problems with sase doctor](https://sase.sh/guides/diagnose-with-doctor/) — Run the read-only diagnostic checks and act on what they report.
- [Find and replay an old prompt](https://sase.sh/guides/find-and-replay-prompt/) — Search prompt history, inspect a past prompt, and launch it again safely.
- [Get automated code review](https://sase.sh/guides/get-automated-code-review/) — Review each change automatically and apply the findings you accept.
- [Hand a result to another agent](https://sase.sh/guides/hand-a-result-to-another-agent/) — Give a follow-up agent a transcript or specific artifact as task context.
- [Guides](https://sase.sh/guides/) — Goal-titled how-to guides for setup, planning, daily work, and fixing problems.
- [Plan a multi-agent change](https://sase.sh/guides/plan-multi-agent-change/) — Turn a large change into a reviewed plan whose phases agents work through.
- [Recover an interrupted agent](https://sase.sh/guides/recover-interrupted-agent/) — Check whether an interrupted agent restarts itself, retry it, or revive it.
- [Reuse a prompt with macros](https://sase.sh/guides/reuse-prompt-with-macros/) — Save a useful prompt as a named macro and use it in later agent runs.
- [Review and land a change](https://sase.sh/guides/review-and-land-change/) — Inspect an agent's result and choose whether to commit, propose, or open a pull request.
- [Run agents in parallel](https://sase.sh/guides/run-agents-in-parallel/) — Split independent work across agents and follow each run from the Agents tab.
- [Schedule recurring work](https://sase.sh/guides/schedule-recurring-work/) — Run a check on a schedule with the scheduler and confirm each run.
- [Set up shell completion and your editor](https://sase.sh/guides/setup-completion-editor/) — Complete sase commands with TAB and edit prompts with language assistance.
- [Unstick a queued agent](https://sase.sh/guides/unstick-queued-agent/) — Tell capacity waits apart from holds and clear whichever blocks the agent.

## Concepts

- [Agents, sessions, and workspaces](https://sase.sh/concepts/agents/) — How SASE gives delegated agent work an isolated place to run and a durable history.
- [Automation and human checkpoints](https://sase.sh/concepts/automation/) — How SASE runs recurring work and keeps important decisions reviewable.
- [How SASE works](https://sase.sh/concepts/) — The small set of ideas that explains how SASE keeps agent work organized and reviewable.
- [How changes land](https://sase.sh/concepts/landing/) — How SASE carries agent changes through review and into version control.
- [Memory and agent instructions](https://sase.sh/concepts/memory/) — How shared instructions and durable context guide agents across tasks.
- [Prompts, macros, and workflows](https://sase.sh/concepts/prompts/) — How one task prompt can grow into reusable instructions and repeatable work.
- [Providers and models](https://sase.sh/concepts/providers/) — How SASE connects agent work to coding-agent providers and models.
- [Work units](https://sase.sh/concepts/work-units/) — How goals, plans, beads, and Patches represent outcomes, coordinated work, and reviewable changes.

## Reference

- [sase's TUI User Guide](https://sase.sh/ace/) — sase's TUI User Guide — sase's TUI is the primary TUI for the SASE toolkit.
- [Agent Attachments and Image Previews](https://sase.sh/agent_images/) — Agent Attachments and Image Previews — SASE treats files produced by agents as first-class completion artifacts.
- [Installing & Authenticating Agent Providers](https://sase.sh/agent_providers/) — Installing & Authenticating Agent Providers — SASE normally orchestrates an existing coding-agent CLI; the exception is the bundled fakey testing provider.
- [Agent Clans, Sessions, and Tribes](https://sase.sh/agent_sessions/) — Agent Clans, Sessions, and Tribes — SASE uses three different kinds of agent grouping.
- [Agent Hood Synchronization](https://sase.sh/agents_sidecar/) — Agent Hood Synchronization — SASE publishes deterministic project-scoped agent-hood snapshots and canonical prompt archives through each managed project's hidden agents sidecar.
- [Artifact Links](https://sase.sh/artifact_links/) — Artifact Links — Artifact links are typed relationships between SASE artifacts.
- [Artifact References](https://sase.sh/artifact_references/) — Artifact References — Artifact references are typed @<kind>:<argument> citations in launch prompts.
- [Scheduler — Background Automation](https://sase.sh/axe/) — Scheduler — Background Automation — The scheduler is the background automation subsystem of sase.
- [Bead Issue Tracking](https://sase.sh/beads/) — Bead Issue Tracking — Bead is a lightweight, git-native issue tracking system built into sase.
- [Patch Format Documentation](https://sase.sh/change_spec/) — Patch Format Documentation — A Patch is SASE's durable local record for one unit of reviewable work.
- [CLI Reference](https://sase.sh/cli/) — CLI Reference — This page is a command index for the top-level sase CLI.
- [Shell Completion](https://sase.sh/completion/) — Shell Completion — sase completion supports native shell completion for zsh, bash, and fish from the live sase argparse tree, so pressing <TAB> anywhere in the command line offers the right commands, options, static choices, and live values — bead ids with titles, project display names, macro names, and more — with no perceptible latency.
- [Configuration Reference](https://sase.sh/configuration/) — Configuration Reference — This document is the central reference for all sase configuration: config files, YAML sections, environment variables, and CLI flags.
- [Editor Integration](https://sase.sh/editor/) — Editor Integration — SASE exposes two editor-facing surfaces for prompt and macro editing:
- [Goals](https://sase.sh/goals/) — Goals — Goals are durable records of outcomes a person wants: what will be true, how you'll know, and what happened along the way.
- [Initialization](https://sase.sh/init/) — Initialization — SASE initialization commands create or refresh durable files that agents and sidecar tools rely on.
- [Instruction Bundles](https://sase.sh/instruction_bundles/) — Instruction Bundles — An instruction bundle collects the project, home, and SASE instructions for one agent invocation.
- [Integration APIs](https://sase.sh/integrations/) — Integration APIs — SASE exposes a small set of Python helpers for external plugins, chat clients, mobile clients, and editor integrations.
- [LLM Provider Integration](https://sase.sh/llms/) — LLM Provider Integration — This document describes the LLM provider abstraction layer in sase.
- [Macro Template Reference](https://sase.sh/macros/) — Macro Template Reference — Macros are reusable prompt templates with optional typed inputs and Jinja2 support.
- [Memory](https://sase.sh/memory/) — Memory — SASE memory is durable context that survives individual agent chats.
- [Memory History](https://sase.sh/memory_history/) — Memory History — Every committed version of every SASE memory note, web, strand, and agent instruction file (AGENTS.md plus its provider shims, project and home) can be browsed quickly and understood at a glance.
- [Mentors](https://sase.sh/mentors/) — Mentors — Mentors are automated AI code review agents for Patches.
- [Mobile Gateway](https://sase.sh/mobile_gateway/) — Mobile Gateway — The SASE mobile gateway is a workstation-hosted HTTP gateway for paired mobile clients.
- [Monitors](https://sase.sh/monitors/) — Monitors — A monitor turn is a real agent session member whose work is one supervised OS command instead of an LLM turn.
- [Notifications](https://sase.sh/notifications/) — Notifications — Sase includes a notification system that surfaces important events from background processes (axe, workflows, mentors) to the user through sase's TUI.
- [SASE Pager](https://sase.sh/pager/) — SASE Pager — sase pager opens artifact references, file paths, or stdin in the SASE link-traversing pager.
- [Plugin System](https://sase.sh/plugins/) — Plugin System — Sase uses Python entry points to discover optional functionality installed in the same Python environment as sase.
- [ProjectSpec Format](https://sase.sh/project_spec/) — ProjectSpec Format — A ProjectSpec is SASE's project-level .sase file.
- [Prompt History and Draft Recovery](https://sase.sh/prompt/) — Prompt History and Draft Recovery — Prompts you launch with sase run or from sase's TUI are recorded in prompt history when they are useful to replay.
- [Query Language Reference](https://sase.sh/query_language/) — Query Language Reference — The Patch query language filters Patches using boolean expressions that combine string matching, property filters, and operational shorthands.
- [Agent auto-restart](https://sase.sh/reference/agent-auto-restart/) — Recovery service for agents interrupted by a live update, and its limits.
- [Agent revive log](https://sase.sh/reference/agent-revive-log/) — Audit records for TUI agent revival, and how to read them.
- [sase agent-cli](https://sase.sh/reference/cli/agent-cli/) — Inspect the coding-agent CLIs supported by SASE and install or update installs whose management method can be identified safely.

- [Sudo Requests](https://sase.sh/sudo/) — Sudo Requests — SASE sudo requests let an agent ask for reviewed privileged execution without ever asking for, receiving, logging, or proxying a password.
- [Named Tools and ToolRuns](https://sase.sh/tool/) — Named Tools and ToolRuns — A named tool is a project-declared command (check, test, ...) that sase tool run executes exactly as declared and records as a ToolRun: who ran it, when, with what result, how long each stage took, and what the repository and host looked like before and after.

- [Workspace Provider Reference](https://sase.sh/workspace/) — Workspace Provider Reference — The workspace provider layer is an abstraction that handles workspace-level operations that vary across VCS hosting environments.

## Contribute

- [Artifacts pane contract](https://sase.sh/artifacts_pane_contract/) — Artifacts pane contract — ArtifactsPaneContract is the host-owned record that decides what a pane can do before widgets, keybindings, or document providers run.
- [Artifacts pane visual grammar](https://sase.sh/artifacts_pane_visual_grammar/) — Artifacts pane visual grammar — Every configured Artifacts pane — Commits, Patches, Beads, Files, every document provider, and a degraded provider that failed to load — renders through one shared, contract-driven shell.
- [Commit Workflows](https://sase.sh/commit_workflows/) — Commit Workflows — Sase provides three unified workflows for landing code changes: commit, propose, and pull request.
- [Acknowledgements](https://sase.sh/contribute/acknowledgements/) — People, projects, and research that shaped SASE.
- [Architecture](https://sase.sh/contribute/architecture/) — Architecture internals, runtime flow, state ownership, and provider boundaries inside SASE.
- [Contribute](https://sase.sh/contribute/) — Contributor guides, internals, contracts, and runbooks for SASE.
- [Reader testing](https://sase.sh/contribute/reader-testing/) — How to run an observed reader round and turn the results into doc changes.
- [Writing docs](https://sase.sh/contribute/writing-docs/) — The sase.sh documentation contract for humans and agents.
- [Development](https://sase.sh/development/) — Development — This page orients contributors working in the sase repository.
- [Fakey Testing Provider](https://sase.sh/fakey/) — Fakey Testing Provider — fakey is a deterministic fake agent CLI bundled with SASE.
- [Mobile MVP Runbook](https://sase.sh/mobile_mvp_runbook/) — Mobile MVP Runbook — This runbook covers the private Android MVP that connects a phone to a workstation-hosted SASE mobile gateway.
- [`sase tui` Performance Runbook](https://sase.sh/perf_runbook/) — `sase tui` Performance Runbook — This runbook explains how to capture and compare performance data for sase's TUI, the sase tui terminal user interface.
- [Rust Backend (`sase_core_rs`)](https://sase.sh/rust_backend/) — Rust Backend (`sase_core_rs`) — A subset of sase's core APIs is served by a Rust extension distributed as sase-core-rs on PyPI and built from the sibling sase-core repo.
- [SDD Storage](https://sase.sh/sdd_storage/) — SDD Storage — The workspace provider owns SDD placement.
- [Telemetry](https://sase.sh/telemetry/) — Telemetry — SASE records debugging and health metric history locally.

## Blog

- [SASE Blog](https://sase.sh/blog/) — Essays on structured agentic software engineering and the SASE launch post.
- [[03] AXE — The Background Daemon That Keeps Agent Work Moving](https://sase.sh/blog/posts/axe-background-daemon/) — Agents shouldn't poll. AXE is the background daemon that does the polling for them so the engineering workflow keeps moving while individual agents finish, fail, or wait.
- [[04] Beads and SDD — Planning Multi-Agent Work That Actually Lands](https://sase.sh/blog/posts/beads-and-sdd/) — Orchestration only matters if you can split work into pieces with a real ordering. Beads and Spec-Driven Development are how SASE files that work and schedules it.
- [[06] Patches in Practice — Review State Outside the Chat](https://sase.sh/blog/posts/changespecs-in-practice/) — Patches are durable, reviewable records for PR-sized agent work. This post shows how their review state works in practice.
- [[05] Commit Workflows — The Pluggable Path From Diff to PR](https://sase.sh/blog/posts/commit-workflows-plugins/) — Every agent eventually has to land code somewhere. SASE's commit workflows are the small, runtime-uniform layer that turns a diff into a commit, a proposal, or a pull request without the agent caring which VCS is underneath.
- [[02] Macros in Depth — From One File to Full Workflows](https://sase.sh/blog/posts/macros-in-depth/) — Macros up close: when a single Markdown file is the right shape, when typed inputs and directives are enough, and when the job really does want a YAML workflow.
- [[08] Where You Type — The Prompt Input Widget and sase-nvim](https://sase.sh/blog/posts/prompt-widget-and-nvim/) — Where the operator actually types: a multiline Textual TextArea with completion, history, snippets, and a Vim mode in the TUI — and sase-nvim, the Neovim plugin that gives the same prompt language a richer editor.
- [SASE: Structured Agentic Software Engineering](https://sase.sh/blog/posts/structured-agentic-software-engineering/) — From a tmux full of coding agents to an operating layer around them: agent CLIs, Macros, sase's TUI Agents tab, and a practical install path for SASE.
- [[07] Driving SASE From Your Phone — Telegram as the Mobile Control Surface](https://sase.sh/blog/posts/telegram-mobile-agents/) — The sase-telegram plugin turns an existing Telegram chat into a mobile control surface for SASE — launch agents, approve plans, kill runs, and review generated images from the phone in your pocket.
- [[09] What's Next — Shared Memory, Mobile, and the Web Surface](https://sase.sh/blog/posts/whats-next-memory-mobile-web/) — SASE today is the orchestration layer. The next horizon is shared memory across agents, a mobile control surface, and a web frontend that doesn't require a terminal.
- [[00] The Missing Operating Layer for Coding Agents](https://sase.sh/blog/posts/why-coding-agents-need-orchestration/) — SASE's first principles: Macros, SDD, Beads, sase's TUI, AXE, plugins, and the durable operating layer around coding-agent CLIs.
